text: his name was Babur. At Panipat, north of Delhi, he faced the Sultan of Delhi, who had a far
bigger army, and around a hundred war elephants. Remember those elephants? For two thousand
years they had decided India's battles. Porus had them, the Nandas had thousands, Chandragupta
traded land for 500. Bobor brought something new. Cannons and muskets. The guns roared,
the elephants panicked, and in a single day, the Sultanate was gone. So was the age of the war
elephant. Bobor founded the Mughal Empire. He also wrote a brutally honest memoir. And honestly,
he was not impressed with India. Your Majesty, the finest mangoes in Hindustan.
Mmm, no melons? Mango's Majesty, everyone loves them.
Mmm, no good horses, no good grapes, no melons.
